name_en: Riccoldo da Monte di Croce (Ricoldo, Ricardus, Riculdus)
born: c. 1243 (brief; NOT VERIFIED in this session)
died: Conflicting: 31 Oct 1309 in Florence per Poccianti, as quoted by Quetif-Echard and reprinted by Laurent 1864 (VERIFIED as a citation in that source); c. 1320 per the 2024 volume title seen in a search result (UNVERIFIED, not opened)
role_place: Dominican friar (Florentine, Santa Maria Novella); spent years in the Near East and at Baghdad (Baldach/Valdacum) studying Arabic and the Qur'an, c. 1288-1300; later in Florence.
why_relevant: Author of the most influential medieval Latin refutation of the Qur'an (Contra legem Sarracenorum), read in manuscript and print for two centuries; also author of the Liber peregrinationis with polemic on Islam.
fame: Well known in the specialist literature on medieval Christian views of Islam; his Contra legem was printed in Seville 1500 (per Ferrero Hernandez 2021), translated into Spanish (1501-1502), retranslated into Latin from Kydones' Greek by Bartholomaeus Picenus (Rome 1506), and reprinted through the 16th century; Luther published a German version in 1542. Not a household name outside specialist circles.
catholic_status: Dominican friar (Order of Preachers). No canonization or beatification found in the sources I read; treat formal status as UNVERIFIED.
notes_on_brief: Brief said c. 1243-1320. Born year: UNVERIFIED. Death: 1320 is CONTRADICTED by the 1864 Laurent intro (1309) but supported by a 2024 volume title seen only in search results; the team should flag this conflict.

role_place: Florentine poet and exile; author of the Divina Commedia.
why_relevant: Places Muhammad and his cousin-in-law Ali among the schismatics of the ninth bolgia of Hell (Inferno XXVIII), the only Islamic figures I found in the Commedia text I read.
fame: Among the best-known works of European literature; the Inferno XXVIII Muhammad scene is a standard anthology and school text (seen in Italian school-summary pages in search results, not opened in depth). The passage is literary punishment imagery, not an argument about Islam.
catholic_status: Catholic layman and poet; no canonical status (not a saint or doctor of the Church).
